rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~97% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~93%; BoJ Dec ~85%; BoE Dec ~82%; BoC Dec ~80%; RBA Dec hold ~99%; IMF backs RBA tightening bias
rows.read: A December Fed hike stays all but certain, and hikes are also widely expected from the European Central Bank, the Bank of Canada, the Bank of Japan and the Bank of England. The International Monetary Fund backed the Reserve Bank of Australia's leaning toward higher rates, which helped the Aussie.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Beige Book: growth in 8 of 12 Fed regions, none declined; Australia Q3 private capex +12.2% q/q (fcst 4.5%); Germany GfK Dec −30.2 (fcst −29.4)
rows.read: Australian firms stepped up investment far more than expected, and the Fed's Beige Book found most US regions still growing. German consumers stayed deeply gloomy. Strong growth backs higher rates in the US and Australia, while Europe lags.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Tokyo core CPI Nov +2.9% y/y (fcst 3.0%, Oct 2.6%), ex-food and energy 2.5% (Oct 2.6%), energy +9.5%; US core PCE Oct +3.3% y/y; Australia CPI Oct 4.9% y/y
rows.read: Tokyo's inflation rose to its highest in 16 months, but mainly because of energy. Prices outside food and energy cooled a little, which backs a December Bank of Japan hike without pushing for a faster pace. US and Australian inflation stay well above goal, keeping both central banks leaning against easing.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Gold ~$3,651 (+2.4%); MSCI Asia-Pacific +0.6%, Nikkei +0.7%, Kospi +1.5% (Bloomberg); Israel security cabinet meeting on Iran cancelled, no decision (Hercules); AUD/USD +0.5%, USD/CHF flat
rows.read: Fear of new Israeli strikes on Iran and more attacks on Gulf shipping sent gold sharply higher overnight. Stock markets did not share the worry, as Asian shares rose for a second day. So the Aussie and kiwi gained while the yen and franc stayed flat.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$96.19, settled $96.57 Thursday (highest since Nov 6), ~+3.9% on the week, ~−18% in November (Reuters); WTI ~$85.96; gold ~$3,651 (+2.4%) (Hercules)
rows.read: Oil held near $96 after its highest close in three weeks, as Gulf attacks kept supply fears alive though no barrels were lost. That helps the Canadian dollar and costs Japan and the euro area. Gold jumped, a lift for Australia, one of its big producers.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Heavy bets against the loonie leave room for a fast unwind if Canadian hike bets keep growing.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: NZ final count: coalition 65 of 130 seats, 66 needed (ABC News); S&P France review Fri Nov 27; US Section 301 tariff proposals on 14 economies, comments due Jan 5 (USTR)
rows.read: New Zealand's final election count left the governing coalition one seat short of a majority, so it must win over a smaller party or face a new vote. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating late on Friday, November 27.
